label: Institution
name: ABC Color
summary:
ABC Color (also known as Diario ABC Color) is Paraguay's most widely read and influential newspaper — founded in 1967 and owned by the Zuccolillo family — representing the most significant independent press institution in Paraguay, a country that only ended 35 years of General Alfredo Stroessner's dictatorship in 1989 and has had a challenging relationship with press freedom and democratic governance. ABC Color has played a significant role in Paraguayan journalism and political life.

Paraguay's media landscape reflects the country's difficult democratic history: Stroessner's 1954-1989 dictatorship was one of South America's longest single-person authoritarian rules, and press freedom was severely constrained throughout. ABC Color was founded in 1967 during the Stroessner era and faced significant government pressure, including forced closure from 1984 to 1989 by the Stroessner government — a period during which the newspaper's critical journalism was suppressed. The newspaper's reopening coincided with the 1989 coup that ended Stroessner's rule.

ABC Color's post-Stroessner role as Paraguay's leading newspaper has involved significant influence over Paraguayan public opinion and political coverage, including coverage of the Colorado Party's continuing political dominance (the Colorado Party ruled Paraguay without interruption from 1947 to 2008, an extraordinary 61-year single-party dominance), and the country's ongoing governance challenges including land inequality (Paraguay has one of the world's most unequal land distributions), corruption, and institutional development.
